questions.q: What does traditional economic theory mean by a rational consumer?
options: Someone who never makes a mistake
Someone who weighs up costs and benefits to get the most satisfaction from their income
Someone who always buys the cheapest option
Someone who saves most of their income
questions.why: Rational means choosing the option that best meets your own aims after weighing costs and benefits. It does not mean perfect or cheapest.

questions.q: A consumer's total utility from {n} cups of tea is {a} units, and from one more cup it is {b} units. What is the marginal utility of the extra cup?
questions.why: {b} − {a} = {answer}. Marginal utility is the change in total utility from one more unit.

questions.q: The marginal utility of the first three slices of cake is {a}, {b} and {c} units. What is the total utility of the three slices?
questions.why: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities: {answer} units.

questions.q: Total utility is at its highest when marginal utility is zero.
questions.why: While marginal utility is positive, total utility is still rising. Once it hits zero, one more unit adds nothing, and below zero total utility falls.

questions.q: Which statement describes the hypothesis of diminishing marginal utility?
options: As more of a good is consumed in a period, total satisfaction falls
As more of a good is consumed in a period, the extra satisfaction from each additional unit eventually falls
As income rises, people buy less of every good
questions.why: It is the extra (marginal) satisfaction that falls. Total utility can go on rising.

questions.q: A student has already revised for two hours. A third hour would be worth £5 to them, but they would give up a £7 shift to do it. What does thinking at the margin suggest?
options: Revise, because the first two hours were useful
Take the shift, because the extra benefit of the third hour is less than its extra cost
Revise, because two hours have already been spent
Take the shift, because revision has no value
questions.why: The choice depends only on the extra benefit and extra cost of the next hour, not on the hours already spent.

questions.q: Explain why diminishing marginal utility supports a downward-sloping demand curve.

ideas.label: Each extra unit gives less satisfaction (marginal utility falls)
So consumers will only buy more at a lower price

questions.model: As more of a good is consumed, each extra unit gives less satisfaction, so marginal utility falls. Because the extra unit is worth less to them, consumers will only buy more if the price is lower, so quantity demanded rises as price falls.
questions.why: Falling extra satisfaction means a lower price is needed to persuade people to buy more.

tests.answer: Each extra unit gives less satisfaction so people will only buy more at a lower price.
Marginal utility falls as you have more of something.
Firms supply more when they can charge more.
